items.title: In three weeks this stops being paper
items.caption:
I'm an engineer, not finance. Six years ago I wrote code that picks stocks the way you'd pick a fantasy team — rules, not hunches — and ran it on paper for six seasons. On 8 October it stops being paper.

This is the pre-season. The next three videos are the flaws I found in my own system. From October, every pick it makes goes up here four weeks after it makes it — wins, losses, red arrows included. A fantasy season where the points are pounds, and they're mine.

Research output, not investment advice. Everything shown is a backtest run on historical data with paper money — no real positions, past or present. I'm an engineer, not a financial adviser, and nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell anything.

items.title: Take out their five best gameweeks
items.caption:
Someone wins your mini-league every year, and every year they explain why. Here's the test that finds out whether they were any good: take their five best gameweeks out.

I ran it on a stock system I built. 35% a year became 17%. The average manager got 15%.

Research output, not investment advice. Everything shown is a backtest run on historical data with paper money — no real positions, past or present. I'm an engineer, not a financial adviser, and nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell anything.

items.title: It's like picking your teams in May
items.caption:
I picked my stocks the way you'd cheat at fantasy football: with the final table already in front of me. Took six years to notice. Here's how the bias got in — and it wasn't through the rules.

Research output, not investment advice. Everything shown is a backtest run on historical data with paper money — no real positions, past or present. I'm an engineer, not a financial adviser, and nothing here is a recommendation to buy or sell anything.

items.title: Deleting the winners didn't reduce the pain
items.caption:
I deleted my five best results. The return halved. The worst run didn't move: −51.3% became −50.9%. The pain was never coming from the trades that worked.
